`work.jsonl` is generated by `tools/generate_work_fixtures.py` against mmx-node
`ca6438b37c08007106d58efe4a990f6ecb276649`. It links the existing native CPU
space-proof libraries and copies the original Node::verify_proof overloads,
verify_proof_impl, difficulty-adjustment checks and ancestor lookup methods with
only their class qualifiers changed. Reference source/data are not modified.

Leaf/memory rows call the native memory hash and compute_f1 directly. Compute
rows compare native compute(..., xbits=0), every final Y/metadata pair and the
canonical 256-X backtrace. Verify/proof rows use the original pos::verify and
Node::verify_proof, including positive OG/NFT witnesses before/after hardfork 1.
Positive witnesses use k8 plots with minimum ksize overridden. Separate leaf
vectors exercise k29/k32. Two witnesses use the normal plot/post-filter sizes
(4/10), with smaller ksize and a test difficulty constant.

Witness discovery uses a copy of compute_full with a 20,000-match cap; exceeding
that cap skips the candidate. This bound affects only fixture discovery. Expected
outputs and acceptance always come from the unmodified native verifier. Plot
creation, compression, GPU/remote compute and production plot files are unused.

Transition rows call the original full header verifier with trusted parent,
challenge, difficulty and per-infusion iteration inputs supplied by the harness.
They cover proof commitments/order/duplicates, limits, hardfork boundaries,
difficulty, challenges, fork counters and both weights. History rows call original
get_challenge/get_infusion over linked synthetic ancestor headers, including gaps.
Context rows combine those native lookups for the candidate's expected inputs.
Headers represent trusted snapshots; verifying the entire synthetic ancestry is
outside these fixtures.

Space-difficulty/challenge/threshold/filter rows call the original utils.h and
pos helpers, covering wrapping arithmetic, 48-bit difficulty clamping, forced
infusion, strict quality boundaries, little-endian 256-bit values and zero/full
filter widths. Pipeline rows combine original header validity/authentication and
space/transition verification; Rust tests additionally prepare the empty body
through the existing settlement API and enforce no publication on rejection.

These fixtures do not verify VDF work/output linkage, NFT reward-target calls,
durable header archives or chain selection. `ProofContext` inputs and HeaderSource
must come from authenticated chain history in a complete node.
